extracted.subtask_description: Checklist of items authors should include when reporting cohort studies to ensure transparent, complete reporting of study design, conduct, analysis, and interpretation (STROBE Statement for cohort studies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Title and abstract (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Indicate the study’s design with a commonly used term in the title or the abstract; (b) Provide in the abstract an informative and balanced summary of what was done and what was found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a commonly understood study-design term (eg 'prospective cohort', 'retrospective cohort') in title/abstract; ensure the abstract gives an informative, balanced summary of methods and main results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Background/rationale (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the scientific background and rationale for the investigation being reported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide context and justification for why the study was conducted, referencing relevant prior work and gaps the study addresses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objectives (Item 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: State specific objectives, including any prespecified hypotheses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly list primary and secondary objectives and any hypotheses planned before analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study design (Item 4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Present key elements of study design early in the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe whether the study is prospective/retrospective, cohort type, time frame, and essential design features near the start of Methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the setting, locations, and relevant dates, including periods of recruitment, exposure, follow‑up, and data collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide geographic and institutional context, calendar dates (start/end of recruitment, follow-up), and any relevant temporal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give the eligibility criteria, and the sources and methods of selection of participants. Describe methods of follow‑up. (b) For matched studies, give matching criteria and number of exposed and unexposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report inclusion/exclusion criteria, how participants were identified/recruited, follow-up procedures, and for matched designs provide matching details and group sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variables (Item 7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define all outcomes, exposures, predictors, potential confounders, and effect modifiers. Give diagnostic criteria, if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide operational definitions, measurement thresholds, and any case/diagnostic definitions used in the study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data sources/measurement (Item 8*)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each variable of interest, give sources of data and details of methods of assessment (measurement). Describe comparability of assessment methods if there is more than one group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State data sources (eg medical records, interviews, registries), measurement instruments, validation/reliability information, and any differences between groups. *Give information separately for exposed and unexposed groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bias (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe any efforts to address potential sources of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report steps taken to reduce selection bias, information bias, confounding, and other systematic errors (eg blinding, standardized measurement, adjustment).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study size (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the study size was arrived at.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe sample size calculations, power considerations, or practical considerations that determined the number of participants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quantitative variables (Item 11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how quantitative variables were handled in the analyses. If applicable, describe which groupings were chosen and why.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State transformation, categorization, and rationale for cut points; report units and scaling used in analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods (Item 12)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Describe all statistical methods, including those used to control for confounding. (b) Describe any methods used to examine subgroups and interactions. (c) Explain how missing data were addressed. (d) If applicable, explain how loss to follow‑up was addressed. (e) Describe any sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide details of modeling approaches, variable selection, adjustment strategy, interaction testing, imputation or other missing-data methods, handling of censoring/attrition, and sensitivity analyses to check robustness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participants — results (Item 13*)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Report numbers of individuals at each stage of study—e.g. numbers potentially eligible, examined for eligibility, confirmed eligible, included in the study, completing follow‑up, and analysed. (b) Give reasons for non‑participation at each stage. (c) Consider use of a flow diagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a participant flow (counts and reasons for exclusions) and consider a flowchart to display recruitment, retention, and analysis sample. *Give information separately for exposed and unexposed groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive data (Item 14*)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give characteristics of study participants (e.g. demographic, clinical, social) and information on exposures and potential confounders. (b) Indicate number of participants with missing data for each variable of interest. (c) Summarise follow‑up time (e.g. average and total amount).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide baseline tables, counts of missing data per variable, and measures of follow‑up duration (mean, median, total person‑time). *Give information separately for exposed and unexposed groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcome data (Item 15*)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report numbers of outcome events or summary measures over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present event counts, incidence rates, means over time, or other appropriate outcome summaries; separate results for exposed/unexposed if applicable. *Give information separately for exposed and unexposed groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Main results (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Give unadjusted estimates and, if applicable, confounder‑adjusted estimates and their precision (e.g. 95% confidence interval). Make clear which confounders were adjusted for and why they were included. (b) Report category boundaries when continuous variables were categorized. (c) If relevant, consider translating estimates of relative risk into absolute risk for a meaningful time period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present effect estimates with measures of uncertainty, report both crude and adjusted results with clear adjustment sets, define categorized variable boundaries, and where useful convert relative measures to absolute risks for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other analyses (Item 17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report other analyses done—e.g. analyses of subgroups and interactions, and sensitivity analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe post‑hoc and planned secondary analyses, interactions tested, and results of robustness checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key results (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarise key results with reference to study objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise summary that ties findings back to the pre‑specified objectives and hypotheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss limitations of the study, taking into account sources of potential bias or imprecision. Discuss both direction and magnitude of any potential bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledge study weaknesses (measurement error, residual confounding, selection bias), their likely direction and size, and implications for interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation (Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give a cautious overall interpretation of results considering objectives, limitations, multiplicity of analyses, results from similar studies, and other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide balanced conclusions, avoiding overstatement; place findings in context of existing literature and limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalisability (Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss the generalisability (external validity) of the study results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the extent to which results apply to other populations, settings, times, and the limits to extrapolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Give the source of funding and the role of the funders for the present study and, if applicable, for the original study on which the present article is based.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose funding sources, sponsorship, and any funder involvement in design, data collection, analysis, interpretation, or reporting.
